setting: The story is set among the chaebol families of a parallel-world, present-day Seoul. Everyday life revolves around business wars, shareholdings, arranged marriages, and the alliances and rivalries between chaebol houses. Romance set against the families' business wars, and the public talk that puts any photographed affair at the top of the business pages, are where the whole story's tension lives.

statNotes.selfId: Rises when she chooses something her family would not have chosen for her, in front of someone who will report it. Falls when she performs the daughter the name requires.
statNotes.secrecy: Falls when the relationship becomes legible to anyone outside the circle - a driver, a house staff member, a photographer outside a hotel, a line in a business column. Rises when a plausible reason is on the record first.
statNotes.mood: Driven by the family's calendar, what the companies are doing to each other this quarter, and how the last exchange with the target member ended.

composed: {name} is the circle these {n} women move in: each of them an heir of a different chaebol house.

{org} is the largest of those houses and the one the others orbit. {name} exists only in this story. These {n} have known each other since childhood - the same schools, the same weddings, the same board dinners - and their families do business with and against each other constantly. Whatever groups these members belong to outside this story are not part of this world and must never be mentioned.

ONLY the members listed in MEMBER PROFILES are named people in this story. Everyone else is unnamed - a driver, a house staff member, an executive, a reporter - and no other name may be used, not even in passing or over a phone.

identities.name: Rival heiress
identities.background: [Identity: Rival Heiress] You are the daughter of another chaebol house, and your family competes directly with {name}'s in the same industry. Typical events: You are seated next to each other at the same banquet and the whole room is watching what you say; Both families bid on the same project and you are looking at her from across the table; A reporter asks for your view of her family and you give an answer with nothing in it; Afterwards she is waiting in the car park, and what she asks about is not business. Advantage: You are her equal - one of the few people in this circle who does not have to look up at her. Disadvantage: Every interaction between you is taken as business first, including the sincere ones. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

identities.name: Fallen heiress
identities.background: [Identity: Fallen Heiress] Your family was once part of this chaebol circle too, and lost everything a few years ago. You still have to face the circle's social life, but your standing is not what it was. Typical events: Someone at a banquet remembers your name, with sympathy in their voice; You are wearing something two seasons old and she says nothing, only stands a little closer to you; Somebody brings up what happened to your family in front of you and she changes the subject; You need a job, and the person who can give you one is sitting opposite. Advantage: You understand this circle's rules better than anyone, because you were once inside it too. Disadvantage: Everyone knows where you stand now, you included - so anything she gives you looks like charity. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

identities.name: New employee
identities.background: [Identity: New Employee] You have just started work at {name}'s family company: an entry-level office worker facing all the challenges of a first job, while {name}, heir to the group, seems - by design or by accident - to be looking out for you. Typical events: You take the directors' private lift by mistake, and when the doors open she is standing inside; One afternoon at your desk, staff from the CEO's office deliver afternoon tea for your whole team; You make a mistake at work through inexperience and she gets you out of it; She takes you along to a chaebol social event. Advantage: Natural contact at work. Disadvantage: The status gap, and the line between work and feelings. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

identities.name: Chief of staff
identities.background: [Identity: Chief of Staff] You are {name}'s new executive secretary in her family's house, in charge of her schedule and of looking after her. Typical events: Late at night in the van it is only the two of you, and in the mirror you watch her take the mask off and show how tired and fragile she is; When she runs into trouble in business, you step past the limits of the job to help her work it out; She takes you along on her private plans. Advantage: You see her as she really is in private. Disadvantage: The status gap, and the line between the work and your feelings. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

identities.name: Personal bodyguard
identities.background: [Identity: Personal Bodyguard] You are {name}'s new personal bodyguard, responsible for her safety and never more than a step from her side. Typical events: After a banquet you take off your suit jacket and put it over the thin evening dress she is wearing; On a formal engagement you have brought flat shoes so she can change out of her heels when she is tired; She slips her schedule and goes out alone, and you know where to find her - and you do not report it; Driving her home at dawn she asks whether you are tired, which nobody has asked before. Advantage: The shortest physical distance of anyone; you are almost never apart. Disadvantage: The status gap, and the line between the work and your feelings. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

identities.name: Journalist
identities.background: [Identity: Journalist] You are a reporter, newly assigned to investigate this family. You got close to her for a story - at least at first. Typical events: You slip into a chaebol banquet and she sees immediately that you do not belong there; Through your time with her you gradually learn things about her family that nobody outside knows; Once she knows who you are she does not call her bodyguards, she sits down and asks what you want to know; The deadline gets closer and you start deleting what you have written. Advantage: You do not belong to the chaebol circle, so you can ask what nobody else dares to. Disadvantage: Your relationship began in a deception - whatever it becomes later, that stays a knot buried inside you. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

identities.name: Main Member's Ex-Girlfriend
identities.background:
[Special Identity: Main Member's Ex-Girlfriend]
- You and {name} were lovers, breaking up years ago due to {reason}
- You still keep {keepsake} to this day
- Now the two families' business has brought you back together: awkwardness, complicated feelings, things left unsaid. Early interactions involve deliberate distance, averted eyes, polite but distant
- People in the circle may or may not know about your past. As the game progresses, you may reconcile or go your separate ways

reason: being young and not knowing better
keepsake: the plane tickets from your trip together as a couple

modes.free: [Story Mode: Free] No authored plot events - the relationship itself is the plot. Affection grows slowly. Focus on details and subtle tension: what is said in front of staff, what is said in the car, what is never said at the table. No rushing into relationship.
modes.romance: [Story Mode: Romance] Ambiguous & Romantic. Natural progression with mutual attraction. Members flirt during Flirting stage.
modes.pressure: [Story Mode: Pressure] Press attention and family obligation higher, secrecy changes doubled. Being seen together carries weight: a photographer outside a hotel, a line in a business column, an engagement someone else has already agreed to.
modes.dramatic: [Story Mode: Dramatic] Light comedic. Love triangle scenes probability doubled. Members compete more openly for your attention.

phases.line: - Phase 1 (Rounds 1-6): First encounters. Dinners and obligations, practised politeness, subtle curiosity. No romantic moves.
- Phase 2 (Rounds 7-14): Repeated encounters. Growing familiarity, conversations in cars, accidental touches, first hints of jealousy.
- Phase 3 (Rounds 15-24): Reality pressure. Press interest, an arrangement made on her behalf, what the families owe each other, duty against feelings.
- Phase 4 (Rounds 25+): Consequences. Established relationship, exposure risk, possible proposal or separation.
